# Ragestar

> Ragestar is an independent, MIT-licensed, provider-agnostic desktop AI client. It bundles
> no model provider, no base URL and no credential: you connect a provider or you do not.
> Windows, macOS and Linux. Current release: 2.2.8.

Ragestar is a shell, not a service. The agent engine is a bundled open-source CLI; this
project supplies the window, the session store and the egress layer. Nothing in it names an
official or endorsed provider, and nothing telephones home.

## Canonical links

- [Source repository](https://github.com/9562295450/Ragestar)

- [Checksums and VirusTotal results](https://9562295450.github.io/Ragestar/checksums.html)
- [Installer SHA-256 list](https://github.com/9562295450/Ragestar/releases/download/v2.2.8/SHA256SUMS.txt)

## What it does

- Sessions and projects stored locally in SQLite under the user profile; fork, move and
  compact from the UI.
- Egress lanes: Direct, Cloudflare WARP, Tor and HTTP proxy. A rotation is recorded only
  after the provider endpoint reports the new address, so a silent fallback is recorded
  as a failure rather than as success. Lanes fail independently; auto-recover is off by
  default.
- MCP servers connect at launch and their tools are callable from the composer.
- Provider-agnostic: any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, configured by the user.

## What it does not do

- No bundled provider endpoint, API key or default model.
- No analytics, telemetry or account system.
- No affiliation with, endorsement by, or support commitment from any upstream project or
  provider.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64, macOS 14+ (arm64 or x64), or Linux x64 (AppImage, deb, rpm).
- A provider endpoint, if you want model replies. The app opens without one.

## Attribution

The bundled engine is derived from the OpenCode CLI (MIT). OpenCode is a community-supported
engine configuration, not an official integration, and Ragestar is not affiliated with,
endorsed by or supported by the OpenCode project. See NOTICE.md in the repository for the full
upstream attribution and the list of changes.

## Licence

MIT. Source and releases are public; the app is built from that source by its own
release workflow.
